the cosmic ray p-air measurements are consistent with the QCD-based parameterization, and that the cosmic ray data do not require any additional soft particle production cross section beyond that predicted by our parameterization.
the proton-air cross sections are well described by Glauber theory at all energies, but the inclusive production cross section is constrained to be σtot(pp→anything)=1.2±0.2 mb.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the proton-air cross section is predicted to increase with energy, with an extrapolated value of about σ(p-air)≈300 b at s≈30TeV.
the proton-proton and proton-antiproton scattering data at high energies are well understood and can be used to predict proton-air scattering cross sections with a precision of 5% or less.
the cosmic ray data are consistent with a soft particle production cross section that is not too far from the asymptotic value of the total cross section.
